self.raw_excerpt:
Self-review (7-point), performed against the final worktree.

1. Does it do what the spec says? Yes — ACs (A)-(G), each pinned by a named test.
   Two ACs were violated by my own intermediate designs ((A) and (C), twice) and
   both regressions are now regression-tested from reproduced failures rather
   than from reasoning.

2. Tests: are they testing behaviour or implementation? Behaviour, and
   deliberately against the PRODUCERS. Three defects in this iterate survived a
   green suite because fixtures modelled a shape no writer emits, so
   test_completion_writers.py drives the real tools as subprocesses in real canon
   order, and _c3_fixtures.history_entries now stamps `at` strictly later than
   `event_at` so no suite can pass by reading the wrong clock.

3. Error paths: every unanswerable state has its own stated reason (missing,
   unreadable, no marker, no completion, no completion under the note's run,
   unreadable anchor, coarse timestamp, overlapping spans). None returns a pass.

4. Docs: docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md and docs/guide.md restate the shipped rule
   including both clocks, all three known bounds, and the per-phase ordering
   exceptions. The spec and mini-plan were corrected three times when the design
   changed under them — that lag was the single most repeated finding against me.

5. Scope: no feature beyond the spec. One deliberate omission (the iterate event
   anchor) is recorded in four places and tracked as trg-1346abbd rather than
   half-done.

6. Security: the marker's four values are rendered unescaped as `key: "..."` and
   C3 now keys on two of them, so build_marker sanitises through marker_value —
   a newline in --reason could otherwise forge `phase`/`timestamp` and
   manufacture a PASS for a phase that wrote nothing.

7. Affected boundaries: table updated to include both --entry-json narrowings,
   the phase_history entry-shape change (two new keys), the iterate ledger as a
   consumed record, run_canon_checks' signature, and the three handoff writes.

Residual concerns I am NOT claiming away: the same-phase strengthening is inert
on the merge target until each phase completes once, and permanently for
iterate. Both are stated in the Confidence Calibration.

plan.raw_excerpt:
External plan review (--mode iterate), two providers.

VERDICT: openai = revise, gemini = degraded (truncated output; its one complete
finding was adopted).

Both providers independently hit the same high-severity hole from different ends,
and it CHANGED THE DESIGN before any code was written.

1. [high, openai R1] A static PIPELINE_PHASES order cannot separate "a later
   phase legitimately superseded this one" from "a stale later-phase marker plus
   a re-run of this phase that wrote nothing" — the second silently SKIPs, which
   is defect 1 again. ADOPTED, design changed: supersession is decided by time,
   and PIPELINE_PHASES was dropped from the design entirely.

2. [high, openai R2] The phase_history contract is assumed rather than stated or
   validated; malformed / absent / duplicate / non-completed entries risk
   permanent false WARNs. ADOPTED: one lib/phase_history.py centralises
   extraction, each failure gets its own stated reason, and tests drive the real
   writers rather than hand-built fixtures only.

3. [medium, openai R3] Two independently written artifacts mean a verifier could
   observe one before the other and emit a transient WARN. ADOPTED as
   verification: the canon steps write the marker, then the completion producer,
   then update-step (which runs the validators), so the record is current at
   check time. "Marker names a run absent from the record" keeps its OWN reason
   so a genuine mid-flight read is legible rather than misattributed.

4. [high, gemini R1] If C3 runs before the current phase's completion is flushed,
   "same phase, older recorded id" false-WARNs. SAME AS R3 — ordering verified,
   distinct reason retained for the absent-from-record case.

Recorded after the fact from the dispositions in the mini-plan's "External plan
review — disposition" table; the review itself ran before implementation.

code.raw_excerpt:
Stage-2 internal code review (shipwright-build:code-reviewer, opus) — THREE rounds.

Round 3 verdict: "Nothing blocking. Ship it." — 2 medium (landmine/doc-accuracy,
not live defects) + 4 low, all addressed below.

Round 1 (3 high, 4 medium, 5 low):
- HIGH F11.md — iterate's own F11 rewrote the tracked handoff with neither marker
  flag, AFTER F5b stamped the marker, so every iterate deleted it at the end and
  C3 reported "no canon marker" for ALL EIGHT canon phases. FIXED.
- HIGH section-doc-update.md — a second, per-SECTION write with the same defect.
  FIXED. Both now guarded by an exact-inventory drift test over plugins/**/*.md.
- HIGH — the marker's timestamp is an EVENT time, not a write time, and the rule
  rested on an unenforced ordering invariant. ACCEPTED; design changed (event_at).
- MED docs asserted an ordering inverted for iterate; MED --phase unvalidated;
  MED BOM/durable_read_text; LOW marker injection via --reason; LOW three copies
  of the marker shape; LOW test asserting live mutable state; LOW warning-text
  churn. ALL FIXED.

Round 2 (2 medium, 5 low):
- MED iterate left out of the clock design AND the >=2 count gate structurally
  inert for it. FIXED — the gate now keys on the anchor's existence.
- MED entry_time's or-chain voided a good `at` behind a broken `event_at`. FIXED.
- LOWs: Stop-hook clause in the phase warning, one-directional shape assertion,
  write-contract regex + >=7 floor, eager marker_timestamp, duplicate --help
  spawns, understated Known bound. ALL FIXED.
- The reviewer explicitly endorsed the decision NOT to buy a bloat-exception ADR
  for the iterate event anchor, noting the bound is mechanically held by a test
  rather than merely narrated.

Round 3 (2 medium, 4 low):
- MED PhaseCompletion.when / entry_time had NO production consumer and a
  docstring that claimed "event anchor" while the code fell back to a wall clock.
  FIXED by DELETING both — verified unused by grep before removal.
- MED the cross-phase branch used the owner's LATEST completion as a proxy for
  "when the note was written". FIXED — it now looks up the owner's completion for
  the run the NOTE names. (Same defect the doubt-reviewer reproduced.)
- LOWs: fixture collapsing the two clocks, orphaned section header, obsolete
  canon comment in verifiers/common.py, untracked follow-up. ALL FIXED; the
  follow-up is now trg-1346abbd.
- The unbounded ledger read per Stop was explicitly ruled shippable (3.45 ms at
  54 entries, once per Stop) and left as-is, recorded.

doubt.raw_excerpt:
Stage-3 adversarial doubt review (shipwright-build:doubt-reviewer, opus) — THREE
rounds. Advisory-must-address; every objection below was reproduced or rebutted
with evidence, never waved off.

Round 1 — 2 high, 4 medium:
- HIGH: the marker's timestamp is latest_event_dt (an EVENT time) while
  phase_history.at is wall clock, and the canon block orders record_event ->
  marker -> append, so the marker is structurally OLDER. On any phase re-run
  where record_event's first-wins dedup meant no new event, C3 accused the phase
  of skipping a step it had just performed — same words as the true positive,
  with a remedy that could not clear it. REPRODUCED end-to-end against the real
  tools, then FIXED (event_at anchor, stamped from the same function).
- HIGH: the same mismatch inverted the cross-phase branch. Folded into the fix.
- MEDs: fixtures never produced a marker the way production does; run-config read
  without durable_read_text; iterate ledger ordering; docs overstating. FIXED.
- Could NOT break: timezone/Z/fractional handling, the day-window model,
  "(no events)" markers, marker.phase empty, the drift guards, the signature
  change. Stated as holding.

Round 2 — 1 high, 4 medium/low:
- HIGH: RecordedTime.after is STRICT, which is only sound where equality means
  "same canon block". Reusing it cross-phase — where equality means two phases
  merely share an anchor, which record_event's permanent dedup makes routine —
  reported the phase that ran LATER as superseded by the EARLIER one. A silent
  SKIP: defect 1 re-opened. REPRODUCED, then FIXED by ordering the two phases'
  wall clocks against each other via the new RecordedTime.later_than.
- MEDs: iterate structurally unable to reach the clock check; docs' ordering
  claim false for build (C1 runs per SECTION); write-contract regex gaps. FIXED.
- Could NOT break: later_than's boundaries (all four quadrants, antisymmetry,
  microsecond representability), marker_value line injection, the events-path
  resolution, retention. Stated as holding.

Round 3 — 1 high, 2 medium, 1 low:
- HIGH: the cross-phase branch ordered against the owner's LATEST completion,
  which equals the note-writing completion only if the owner rewrote the note
  then — the very proposition C3 verifies. Reachable through finalize_bundle's
  own F5c -> F5b abort path. FIXED — the owner's completion is now looked up for
  the run the NOTE names, with its own stated reason when there is none.
- MED: "latest" is positional. INVESTIGATED and largely rebutted —
  shipwright_run_config.json is NOT in .gitattributes' union-merge set, so a
  concurrent append conflicts loudly rather than interleaving. The assumption is
  now named in the module rather than left implicit.
- MED: the anchor gate is inert on the merge target and decays only per phase.
  ACCEPTED and stated as an honest limit in the Confidence Calibration.
- LOW: three unsynchronised reads. Left, recorded.
- Could NOT break: later_than's boundaries (again), and the recorded iterate
  bound — every path it attacked lands on an id mismatch the run-id branch
  catches. It qualified the bound's SCOPE, which is now stated.

external_code.raw_excerpt:
External code review (external_review.py --mode code, openrouter): openai =
revise, gemini = degraded (reply truncated by the provider; its complete portion
raised no findings). Run against the FINAL diff after three internal rounds.

openai raised 5 medium findings. Three fixed, two dispositioned with reasons:

1. FIXED — a date-only marker timestamp was parsed as midnight, so the marker was
   the one place still fabricating an instant after HIGH-1 removed it everywhere
   else. The marker now parses through the same precision-preserving reader, and
   a day-precision marker is a stated WARN rather than a confident verdict.
2. FIXED — a malformed `event_at` was indistinguishable from an absent one, so a
   corrupt record silently bought the run-id fallback and disabled the stale-note
   check. PhaseCompletion now carries `claims_anchor`, and present-but-unreadable
   is its own stated WARN. Absent (a pre-change entry) still uses the run id.
3. FIXED — the test that locked in finding 2's behaviour now asserts the WARN,
   with a separate test for the genuinely-legacy no-key case.
4. DISPOSITIONED — "the equal-clock invariant is not guaranteed under concurrent
   activity". True in principle: an event landing between the marker write and
   the completion append would make the anchors differ. The round-2 doubt review
   traced every event producer and found none fires inside that window, and
   crucially the resulting WARN SELF-HEALS (re-running the C3 step re-derives
   latest_event_dt, which now includes the intruding event) — unlike the defect
   it replaced, whose remedy could never clear it. Left as-is, recorded.
5. FIXED — and this one was mine: docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md claimed the iterate
   ledger "stamps the same event_at anchor there" after I had REVERTED that code.
   A doc asserting the opposite of the code is exactly the AC-(F) failure this
   iterate exists to close, re-committed in the same change. Corrected to state
   that iterate stamps no anchor and why.

Note on standing: external review found 5 findings on a diff that three internal
rounds had already passed, and finding 5 was a live AC-(F) violation. The
converse also held — the internal cascade found three HIGHs external review did
not. Neither substitutes for the other.
